Mahsa Amini’s death while in the custody of Iran’s “morality police” is spilling forth the language and tactics of a feminist revolution with reverberations in movements like #MeToo and the fight for abortion rights. https://t.co/B5i5KUJqCa

The Hollywood Commission, launched in the wake of the #MeToo movement, has launched a new survey that aims to address the persistent problems within the power structures of the entertainment industry. https://t.co/fs2Qo9bCzl

In the wake of #MeToo, the assumption was that Hollywood would never be the same. But five years later, how much have things really changed?

@Joypress investigates: https://t.co/NFqY8qy8oz

“#MeToo is a bit of a failure in terms of institutional power,” one television showrunner tells VF. “They mostly didn’t put women in charge, with some exceptions.”

🔗: https://t.co/pyyiuatctt https://t.co/KDJoTLa5jJ

That doesn’t mean that #MeToo hasn’t had an impact on the industry.

“I think what has changed is I think men are afraid,” says a veteran film producer. “It would be nice if that wasn’t the only motivation for behavior to improve. But I’ll take it.” https://t.co/Ej89yBE2D5
